label: ENISA — Severity assessment of personal data breaches
citation: ENISA with the Data Protection Authorities of Greece and Germany, Recommendations for a methodology of the assessment of severity of personal data breaches, v1.0, 20 December 2013
body: ENISA, working with the Greek and German data protection authorities, published a methodology for assessing the severity of personal data breaches that can be used both by DPAs and by data controllers. Its defining feature is the perspective: severity is graded by the impact on the individuals whose data was breached — driven by the type of data involved (the data processing context), how identifiable the individuals are (ease of identification), and aggravating circumstances of the breach — rather than by the damage to the organization. The output is a graded severity level (from low through very high) that scales the response.

This wizard follows that graded, individual-first approach; the specific five-level ladder and the Low / Medium / High / Critical mapping used here are Advokat Frida's general-purpose adaptation (see the outcome text), not figures prescribed by the ENISA document.
